newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Strike threat still looms for Brazil's Santos port.
newsitem.headline: Strike threat still looms for Brazil's Santos port.

text.p: Stevedores at the key Brazilian port of Santos continued to occupy two vessels at the private terminal of steel company Companhia Siderurgica Paulista (Cosipa) and port authorities said a fresh strike could erupt at any time.
The rest of the port was operating normally although light rains were interrupting normal loading of grains, which continued through the morning in dribs and drabs as the weather allowed.

Twenty-six people have been occupying the two ships docked at the Cosipa pier since Wednesday of last week, when they began a three-day strike in protest against a ruling allowing the steel company to use its private workers to conduct loading and unloading at the terminal.

A third vessel was scheduled to dock at the Cosipa pier on Tuesday, according to the port authority Codesp, and stevedores vowed to resume striking if the company conducts its own loading and unloading for the vessel.
A port official said it was possible another strike would halt the port as early as Wednesday if Cosipa went ahead with the operation.
"Today, no, but probably it would spread to the port tomorrow," the spokesman said. "If Cosipa operates it's a fresh strike."

A spokeswoman for the steel company said she had no knowledge of any vessel expected at the private terminal today and reiterated that the firm had no fresh position. Cosipa has not held any talks with stevedores since the beginning of the strike last week.
Abelardo Fernandes, president of the National Stevedores Union, said it now appeared as if no talks would be held with the company.

The stand-off between the stevedores and Cosipa is being watched over by a group of military policemen on the company's pier, but one of the stevedores occupying the boats said he was confident there would be no violent clashes.
"I am confident we will reach an agreement," he said in a telephone conversation.
